description: Not a thing that thinned — a thing that was emptied. What falls when it breaks is a mask, and the masks all match.
lore: Everything else out there is running on habit — a shape walking its round with the details gone, that will only hurt you for standing in the round. Grinmask stops when you stop and starts when you start. It plays. Crackers who work the eastern ground will take any two of anything else before one of these, because the rest defend themselves and this one has intentions, and the intentions did not come from the shape.

Break it and the dark is simply not there any more — no struggle, no leaving. What comes down is the mask, and the mask does not thin. [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] drew one for the Chronicle, and two winters later drew another, off a beast broken thirty miles from the first. She laid the new tracing over the old: line onto line, the whole way round. The same face. Smiling, both times — they are always smiling. And the inward side is smooth as a bowl. Not a face something wore. A face something made.

Those two drawings are most of the reason there is an [[lore/the_hole_under_the_mountain|investigation]] at all. Bettany, who has interviewed half the country about the worst day of its life without flinching, keeps both masks face-down in a drawer now, and has stopped drawing them.
gm_notes: Anchor of the Hollowed and pointer for beat B6 (hinted): ship only that the masks are alike, made not worn, and always smiling — never whose face, never why. The die animation is canon: the creature goes, the mask falls. The Hollowed stay frightening; do not soften this one into sad.
